dimensions.assessment: Directly affects all manufacturers of covered internet-connected consumer devices and provides pre-purchase disclosures for consumers.
dimensions.evidence: Each manufacturer of a covered device shall disclose, clearly and conspicuously and prior to purchase, whether the covered device manufactured by the manufacturer contains a camera or microphone

dimensions.assessment: Requires labeling or disclosure adjustments for qualifying smart devices without banning products or altering core device functions.
dimensions.evidence: disclose, clearly and conspicuously and prior to purchase, whether the covered device manufactured by the manufacturer contains a camera or microphone

dimensions.assessment: Does not appropriate federal spending, relying on existing FTC enforcement mechanisms and administrative guidance.
Establishes a new federal consumer protection disclosure standard enforced under FTC rules, with specific exemptions for standard electronics like phones and laptops.
dimensions.evidence: A violation of section 2 shall be treated as a violation of a rule defining an unfair or deceptive act or practice prescribed under section 18(a)(1)(B) of the Federal Trade Commission Act

dimensions.assessment: Establishes a permanent regulatory requirement for all newly manufactured covered devices produced after the implementation date.
dimensions.evidence: This Act shall apply to all covered devices manufactured after the date that is 180 days after the date on which guidance is issued by the Commission

importance_detail.rationale: The bill imposes a new disclosure requirement on manufacturers of internet-connected consumer devices containing cameras or microphones, enforced nationally by the Federal Trade Commission.
